pending_qa.q: Why do most project failures occur after a contract is signed?
pending_qa.r: Project failures often stem from the inability of teams to act on problems they know how to fix because of contractual boundaries, organisational boundaries, lack of authority, or values that prioritise commercial outcomes over actual project success. Ackroyd emphasises that contracts alone cannot solve the core issue of mobilising individuals to work effectively together within a collaborative framework.

pending_qa.q: How can predictable relationship management improve project productivity?
pending_qa.r: Scottish Water's research comparing projects utilising collaborative working versus those that did not showed that projects with collaborative working experienced significantly reduced delay times. This was attributed to the fact that everybody knew how everyone in the enterprise would respond to emergent issues, allowing organisations to pre-plan and be predictive in handling unforeseen problems.

pending_qa.q: What happens when teams take a claims-focused approach instead of collaborative problem-solving?
pending_qa.r: Australia spends more of the project budget on claims than any other nation in the Western world, according to Ackroyd. This claims-focused mindset, where parties look for leverage and hold back discovered problems for future use, erodes trust and makes people defensive about contractual certainty rather than focusing on achieving the shared project objective.

pending_qa.q: How should teams respond to emergent complexity discovered during project execution?
pending_qa.r: In a collaborative environment, when new complexity or problems arise—whether contaminated ground discovered during excavation or corroded equipment—the response should be predictable, with team members reaching in to fix issues as a shared responsibility rather than assigning blame or seeking contractual claims, allowing paperwork and formal changes to follow resolution.

pending_qa.q: Why must collaborative working culture be designed to be enduring beyond individual relationships?
pending_qa.r: Personal relationship-based collaboration is fragile because it depends on individuals remaining in their roles and understanding the underlying culture. By building the relationship management system into processes and values that exist independent of individual contributors, collaboration survives personnel changes, different project phases, and new stakeholders joining the effort.
